issues.description: Transport and timeout failures from httpx are not caught, retried, or wrapped in the client's typed error model.
Resource IDs are interpolated directly into URL paths without escaping, so IDs containing '/' or reserved characters alter the requested route.
Retry-After values bypass backoff_cap, allowing a server response to force arbitrarily long client sleeps.
Retry-After parsing only supports numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date headers.
Pagination accepts malformed success bodies and silently treats missing items as an empty page.
Batch-create success parsing assumes results is present and well formed, with no validation of result count, uniqueness, or index range.
BatchItemResult does not validate status/task/error invariants, allowing impossible result states into user code.
Scripted mock responses are returned before API-key validation, so tests using enqueue_response can accidentally bypass auth behavior.
Development tooling only declares pytest; no linting, formatting, or type-checking tool is configured despite a typed-client API surface.
Package version is duplicated manually and can drift between project metadata and runtime __version__.
